author: Zak Failla
title: Ricky Lamot Died Trying To Help Co-Worker During Deadly Manassas Shooting, Family Says - NewsBreak
text:
By Zak Failla ,
6 hours ago
Ricky James Lamot spent his life looking out for others. His family says he died doing exactly that when violence erupted at his Virginia workplace .
The 48-year-old Bealeton father of two was among two employees killed during a shooting at United Rentals in Manassas on Wednesday, Sept. 30, and now his loved ones are sharing new details about what they say happened in his final moments.
According to a GoFundMe organized by extended family members, Lamot was trying to help a co-worker during the violent confrontation when he was fatally shot.
The fundraiser describes his actions as a reflection of the man his family knew: someone who put others before himself.
The shooting played out shortly after 7 a.m. at the United Rentals facility on Wellington Road, where police say 37-year-old Marvin Grant, a fellow employee, opened fire following an apparent confrontation.
According to Manassas Police Chief Douglas Keen, Grant had reportedly warned a co-worker that three people were going to die before pulling a handgun and opening fire.
Lamot and 33-year-old Christopher Serrano were killed , while a third employee was wounded and hospitalized.
Grant fled before officers arrived, setting off a search that stretched into the Shenandoah Valley.
Virginia State Police eventually located him along I-81 in Augusta County, where a pursuit ended with Grant pulling over and pointing a gun at his own head.
He later died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The motive behind the workplace shooting remains unclear more than a week later.
For Lamot's family, the tragedy took away a husband, father, brother, son, and coach whose influence stretched far beyond the workplace where he spent his final hours.
Ricky Lamot
GoFundMeHe and his wife, Barbara, had been married for 26 years and raised two children, Haley and Preston. But his family wasn't the only one he helped shape.
A longtime youth sports coach, Lamot devoted countless hours to mentoring young athletes, coaching football and wrestling while teaching lessons that had little to do with the final score.
According to his obituary , he believed coaching was about building confidence, discipline, friendships, and helping children learn to overcome challenges.
He also made an impression on the adults around him.
Keen, who coached youth football alongside Lamot, spoke personally about the loss in the aftermath of the shooting.
"I lost somebody I coached youth football with," Keen said, describing Lamot as a devoted family man whose death struck close to home. "Knowing what his commitment was and knowing his children are now fatherless, it hits home. It hits home for our community."
Among those mourning him is Gabriela Lopez, a United Rentals colleague who said Lamot became far more than a mentor after she joined the company as a young woman.
Over the years, she said, he watched her grow, encouraged her, and helped shape the person she became.
Now expecting her first child on Oct. 31, Lopez said she was unable to travel from New Jersey to Virginia for his Thursday, Oct. 8 memorial gathering. She had invited him to her baby shower just three weeks earlier.
Another longtime colleague, Jason Welsh, recalled more than two decades of friendship with Lamot, including the time they bowled together and won a league championship.
Welsh remembered a man who coached football and wrestling while making a lasting impression on the people around him at United Rentals.
Decker Gottlieb, who worked with Lamot for more than 12 years, said Lamot wasn't his direct supervisor but was still someone he admired as a leader, friend, and family man.
Gottlieb described the days following the shooting as an emotional roller coaster for the United Rentals team, which was mourning both Lamot and Serrano.
The memories weren't all about work or sports.
Lamot's nephew, Michael Baldwin Jr., recalled being caught throwing rocks at cars as a child, prompting his uncle to chase him around the front yard for what he remembered as a good 30 minutes.
Years later, Baldwin credited his uncle with helping shape the man he became.
Others remembered golf trips to Myrtle Beach, his quick wit, and the way he could make an ordinary moment memorable.
The tributes have continued pouring in as the family prepares to say goodbye.
Loved ones gathered for a visitation on Thursday, Oct. 8, at Pierce Funeral Home in Manassas, where guests were encouraged to dress comfortably in keeping with Lamot's personality and his family's wishes.
Rather than flowers, the family suggested donations to Fauquier Youth Football, the Fauquier County Roller Hockey League, or Liberty Athletic Boosters, organizations that reflected his commitment to young athletes and his community.
Meanwhile, the fundraiser organized by Kiley Morgan is helping Barbara and the children with funeral expenses, household bills, groceries, and other financial burdens following his death.
Morgan said in a recent update that the fundraiser is expected to close this weekend, thanking supporters for the generosity shown to the family.
For Lopez, one of the hardest parts of saying goodbye has been remembering the last words Lamot sent her.
It was a simple message about the exciting chapter ahead as she prepared to become a mother.
"Very exciting times ahead. Proud of you kid."
Words she says she'll cherish forever.

The shooting played out shortly after 7 a.m. at the United Rentals facility on Wellington Road, where police say 37-year-old Marvin Grant, a fellow employee, opened fire following an apparent confrontation.
